restrictions: Applies to the selected target poseidon-orchard-r1-prefix-v1 only (one partial round plus the eight fixed full rounds); the construction relies on the first two full rounds being skippable on a line and gives no claim for other round counts.

The run is probabilistic: at most two independent centres on two different lines; the claimed success probability is for the whole run, with the implemented halts of proof.md section 4 counted as failures, and follows from the measured per-centre success rate (lower end of its 95% interval).

heuristics.statement: Each centre of the program (a uniform 254-bit centre c on a line j, odd-part polynomial g_c, roots of G = gcd(g_c, S^((p-1)/2) - 1)) succeeds with probability at least q = 0.318, independently of the other centre; two centres on two different lines then succeed with probability at least 1 - (1 - q)^2 = 0.534, claimed as 0.53.
heuristics.scope: The program of proof.md section 4 at the selected target with at most two centres on lines (j0 + k) mod 3; fresh independent random words per centre (the sample used a deterministic generator for c).
heuristics.extrapolation: From 65 complete single-centre executions at the selected target (28 successes, rate 0.431, Wilson 95% interval [0.318, 0.552]; lines pooled: line 0: 8 of 22; line 1: 9 of 21; line 2: 11 of 22) to the true per-centre rate: the lower end of the interval is used as q. The sample runs used the line rule j = seed mod 3, so all three lines are represented; the program uses two different lines per run.
heuristics.limitations: A 95%% interval fails to contain the true rate about 5%% of the time (its lower end is too high about 2.5%% of the time); the 65 runs are not independent of the build (26 with an earlier build of identical arithmetic); the certificates show only that found roots yield collisions. The Poisson(1/2) root-count model (rate 0.3935) is context only and is not used for the claim.

heuristics.statement: The counts of proof.md sections 6 and 7 are the totals of an instrumented execution of the program whose complete source is in proof.md section 10, under the stated rules: 1 per field operation, 1 per element load or store plus 1 address operation, 3 per loop iteration plus 2 per loop exit, 1 per other executed index or control operation (shift, mask, add, multiply, modulo, compare, branch), 237 per reduced permutation evaluation of stage B, and a 16-word register file per transform block as the only register assumption.
heuristics.scope: All stages of the program of proof.md section 4 at the target dimensions (m = 39062, N = 98304, N' = 49152, H = 49152).
heuristics.extrapolation: None beyond the executed dimensions; the worst case for two centres is formed from the measured data-independent stages and the implemented budgets of the data-dependent stages.
heuristics.limitations: The counts are produced by the instrumentation written into the source; the source is part of the proof text and was not run by the organizer. Word-level costs outside the stated rules (cache, bandwidth) are not part of the model; the control charges are written next to the statements they price.

heuristics.statement: The half-gcd stage on (g, R - 1) stays within 8,800,000,000 charged operations (about 1.5 times the largest observed cost); the stage has this budget as an implemented halt, a halt counts as a failure of the run, and the worst-case total charges the full budget for every centre.
heuristics.scope: Stage D of proof.md section 4 for inputs produced by stages B and C.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the 2 centres of the ledger run (stage totals 5,850,477,654 to 5,850,480,330) to all inputs; exceeding the budget requires a non-normal remainder sequence (probability about 1/p per step) or a gcd of large degree.
heuristics.limitations: Cost concentration is observed and argued, not proved; the budget itself bounds the loss.
